newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close down on heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close down on heavy trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed lower on Tuesday pulled down by investors trimming overweight positions in bank shares, brokers said.
"We are seeing some sizeable switching, from the banks into property shares," said Glenn Lesko, head of equities trading at HG Asia. "Both overseas and local investors were active today."
The Hang Seng Index closed 57.20 points lower at 13,450.08, but well off the morning low of 13,405.20.
Turnover was a heavy HK$10.26 billion, slightly higher than Monday's HK$9.91 billion.
Brokers said the market was selling on the good news of HSBC Holdings' 25 percent rise in net earnings, which was slightly better than the market's forecast of 24 percent.
Index heavyweight HSBC Holdings lost HK$2.50 to close at HK$186.50.

Subsidiary Hang Seng Bank, whose results were slightly disappointing, slumped HK$4.25 percent to HK$84.75. Analysts said the bank's bad debt provisions were more than twice what they had expected. The bank posted earnings growth of 6.3 percent in 1996.
Utilities were the best performers, followed by properties.
Hongkong Telecom added HK$0.20 to HK$13.75, while China Light shed HK$0.20 to HK$35.50.
In the property sector Sun Hung Kai Properties leaped HK$1.00 to HK$91.75, but Cheung Kong lost HK$1.00 to HK$75.75 after touching its all time of HK$78.00 in early trade.

Interest in the property sector was being fueled by speculation that the sales price of units in Cheung Kong's new residential development, to be offered next week, would set a new higher benchmarket for the physical market, brokers said.
Among the most actively traded issues was China Aerospace which added HK$0.125 to HK$2.80 on trade of HK$454.47 million.
The company announced on Tuesday it would be placing a total of 223.2 million new shares to raise HK$535 million to develop a satellite broadcasting system.
Hang Seng Index futures continued to trade at a discount to the cash market. The March contract slipped 55 points to 13,430 in active trade of 13,500 contracts.
